messages:
alex_gpu: heads up — noticed a correlated increase in Xid 13 + ECC warnings on several eu-west-1 A10 nodes starting ~02:10UTC. allocation spike from tenant 'search-labs' around that time. :eyes:
maria_infra: ugh. do we have node-level telemetry tied to tenant routing for those timestamps? can we slice by queue + batch size?
ops_bot: alert: nvidia_xid_rate{code=\"13\",region=\"eu-west-1\"} > baseline threshold (5m avg). first seen 2765439800
samir_sre: can you paste a sample kernel log? also curious if NVLINK/PCIE errors show up.
alex_gpu: quick syslog grab attached below — snippet from gpu-node-42 at 02:12UTC:
```
Mar 05 02:12:31 gpu-node-42 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 13, PID=21984, GPU=0, Channel ID=7, reason: PTE-/TLB-invalidate
Mar 05 02:12:31 gpu-node-42 kernel: nvidia 0000:03:00.0: GPU is lost: GPU reporting system error.
Mar 05 02:12:32 gpu-node-42 kernel: pcieport 0000:01:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=00e0
```
maria_infra: looks like corrected PCIE AERs right before Xid. could be transient link flakiness amplified by a tenant's large-batch workload. lee_ml — any heavy prefills or KV cache patterns from search-labs?
lee_ml: search-labs was running a nightly rerank sweep with batch_size=64 and aggressive prefill (prefixes ~2k tokens). we ramped their traffic for evals last night. suspect high seq len + big batches.
samir_sre: hypothesis: bursty long-seq workloads push the driver/PCI fabric into more AERs -> Xid 13. two-prong: hardware link flake OR driver pressure from large PMAs. action: reproduce on staging with same batch shape. alex, can you run a soak with that profile on a spare node?
alex_gpu: starting a soak now on staging-a10-07 with same batch_shape + tenant tag. I'll push prom tags so we can correlate Xid -> tenant.
ops_bot: note: automated drain policy will not trigger for corrected AER unless Xid >= threshold_count (default 3 in 10m). current nodes are at 1-2.
maria_infra: small ops note — we should avoid mass drains in eu-west during peak billing window. prefer targeted cordon + repro.
lee_ml: also worth validating quantization path. some int8 kernels behave differently with long contexts — might stress the mmu. i'll add a quick compare run (float32 vs int8).
samir_sre: triage checklist (short):
- collect `dmesg | grep -i nvrm` and `journalctl -k` for Xid lines
- nvml logs: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,enc,dec --format=csv -l 1` during soak
- pcie AER counters: `ethtool -S`/lspci to check link errors
- tenant routing logs to map requests -> card
- driver version + kernel changelog
please add any that I missed.
alex_gpu: adding steps to runbook, also enabling a temporary metric: `xid_by_tenant{tenant=~\".*\"}` via our proxy that tags requests with card id. will backfill 6h.
maria_infra: if staging repros, we should schedule a controlled rotate for any node that gets 3 Xid13 in <30m. else leave and monitor.
lee_ml: early result from float32 vs int8 test: int8 run produced 2x memory page faults under same profile. sending logs to thread.
samir_sre: OK — that tilts it toward kernel/driver + workload mix rather than pure HW. still need to rule out flaky PCIe lanes. proposal: run the staging soak under a driver with the recent NV patch (candidate build r535-rc). rollback plan ready.
alex_gpu: running soak with r535-rc on staging now, tagging runs. ETA 1h for decent sample.
maria_infra: heads up to infra oncall — no mass remediation until we confirm. if staging shows lower Xid while r535-rc + float32, then plan: (1) grad driver deploy to small canary in eu-west (3 nodes), (2) monitor xids & AERs, (3) if stable, expand.
ops_bot: action logged: incident-sweep ticket #INC-2026 created for tracking. assigned to @samir_sre.
samir_sre: thanks. i'll own canary and rollback. alex — ping when staging finishes and paste the soak prometheus graphs. :white_check_mark:
alex_gpu: will do. initial soak patch deployed 02:18UTC. collecting metrics.
lee_ml: added a prompt-level mitigation doc: reduce prefill when batch_size>32 for search-labs until we confirm. sending a PR to routing rules.
maria_infra: great. low friction timeline: repro -> canary (3 nodes) -> evaluate 6h -> expand or rotate cards. keep thread updated. :rocket:
